_docs: Defaults for the POC-2 rule engine (D-08: deterministic rulebook, thresholds configurable). Every threshold below documents its source in _sources. This file is the baked-in default config; loadConfig(configPath) deep-merges an optional user override file on top of this one.

_sources.titleMinChars: Screaming Frog SEO Spider default 'Page Titles' min length filter (30 chars)
_sources.titleMaxChars: Screaming Frog SEO Spider default 'Page Titles' max length filter (60 chars)
_sources.titleMaxPx: Screaming Frog default max pixel width for title (~561px desktop Google SERP truncation estimate)
_sources.descMinChars: Screaming Frog default 'Meta Description' min length filter (70 chars)
_sources.descMaxChars: Screaming Frog default 'Meta Description' max length filter (155 chars)
_sources.descMaxPx: Screaming Frog default max pixel width for meta description (~985px desktop Google SERP truncation estimate)
_sources.thinContentWords: POC threshold (brief §6b seeds): chosen to cleanly separate the seeded thin-content fixture (/blog/trail-snacks, 35 words) from normal site copy (100+ words); below common full-suite editorial guidance of 300+ words
_sources.lowTextRatio: General SEO-tooling guidance range for low text-to-HTML ratio (10-25%); no single canonical Screaming Frog figure, documented POC judgment call at the low end
_sources.slowPageMs: Brief §6b seed default (2000ms); matches commonly-cited informal 'slow page' response-time bucket used by SEO crawlers
_sources.redirectChainMax: Screaming Frog 'Redirect Chains' report flags any chain longer than 1 hop
_sources.nearDupWordCountDeltaPct: DEPRECATED (slice C3): superseded by nearDupSimilarity, a real MinHash/Jaccard score. Left as-is, no longer read by near-duplicate-content.
_sources.nearDupSimilarity: slice C3: 5-word-shingle MinHash+LSH estimated Jaccard threshold. 0.75, not the originally-planned 0.9 -- the seeded near-dup fixture pair (/blog/winter-hiking-checklist vs /blog/winter-day-hike-checklist, manifest #18) measures ~0.824 true Jaccard at shingle size 5, so 0.9 would silently miss it; 0.75 leaves margin below that measurement while staying well above the near-zero overlap unrelated same-length pages produce.
_sources.weakInlinkCount: spec.md A4 scope: pages with exactly 1 inlink are 'weakly-linked'
_sources.jsOnlyContentRatio: content-requires-javascript: share of the RENDERED word count that must be absent from the raw HTML before a page counts as render-dependent. 0.5 (half the copy) is a deliberately conservative bar -- the four render-escalated pages in storage/runs that carry a real divergence measure 0.98-1.00, so the finding stays about pages that are genuinely empty without JS, not pages with a JS-injected sidebar. Paired with thinContentWords as an absolute floor so a tiny page cannot clear the ratio on a handful of words.
_sources.excessiveLinksCount: Kishan's rules.js 'excessive-links': >300 internal+external links on one page usually signals a mega-menu or unpaginated archive rather than a deliberate choice.
_sources.deepPageDepth: Kishan's rules.js 'deep-page': depth > 4 clicks from the start URL reads as buried and gets crawled/ranked less.
_sources.soft404MaxWords: Kishan's rules.js 'soft-404': <=120 words AND 404-style title/H1 wording on a 200 status -- a real 404 page dressed up as a normal response.
_sources.longContentNoSubheadingsWords: Jemish's score.ts 'no-subheadings': >300 words with <=1 subheading (h2+h3) has nothing breaking up the copy.
_sources.emptyAnchorRatioMax: Jemish's score.ts 'no-anchor-text': share of a page's internal links with blank anchor text past which the ratio itself is the finding (not just one link).
_sources.noCompressionMinBytes: Kishan's rules.js 'no-compression': absent Content-Encoding is only worth flagging once the response is big enough to matter (>2000 bytes).
_sources.fleschReadingEaseMin: Jemish's analysis.ts 'readability': Flesch Reading Ease < 30 is his own easeBand() cutoff for 'very hard -- postgraduate'.
_sources.oversizedHtmlBytes: Kishan's rules.js 'oversized-html' (site rule): 500KB HTML document, before subresources.
_sources.healthErrorWeight: Health score: damage points a failing error-severity check costs at full reach. 10/3/1 gives every severity step roughly 3x the weight of the one below, so one error outweighs three warnings or ten notices and a wall of notices can no longer dilute a genuine error.
_sources.healthWarningWeight: Health score: damage points a failing warning-severity check costs at full reach (rationale under healthErrorWeight).
_sources.healthNoticeWeight: Health score: damage points a failing notice-severity check costs at full reach (rationale under healthErrorWeight).
_sources.healthHalfScoreDamage: Health score saturation constant k in score = 100 x k/(k + damage). Set equal to healthErrorWeight, i.e. the anchor is 'one error-severity defect on every page it could be checked on halves the score'. Saturating rather than subtractive so two badly-broken sites still rank against each other instead of both pinning to 0 -- the failure that made the pre-1.0 model useless.
